Technically, there is no clearance above Top Secret. There are tons of rumors about supposed clearances above TS, but nothing acknowledged. There are lots of "codeword" types of access controls. Supposedly VRK (very restricted knowledge) and ECI (exceptionally controlled information) exist. Gamma, HCG, Talent Keyhole, etc. are all types of SAP access controls, which requires an individual read on and sometimes a single scope background investigation. TS does not require a poly, but SCI adjudication almost always does, either a CI or FS poly, as does access into to codeword information.

They are different levels but in reality they technically are above top secret with more stringent requirements per given situation. I know first hand what TS clearance demands and it can be a pain given the level.

When you complete your SF86, the package is submitted for one of several clearances - Public Trust, Secret, or Top Secret, that's it. Once you have been adjudicated for TS, you may be eligible for SCI access. Once access has been determined and suitability has been investigation, then you have SCI eligibility. The program requiring SCI may have further requirements, such as a poly. Once this step is completed, you can then be read on via-NDA to an SCI level program. If that program requires further access - satellite (TK), HUMINT (HCG), or other type, that then requires another NDA and possibly another SSBI by that specific team. Regardless, you will still only have a TS clearance, it will just be entered into JPAS as TS w/ SCI eligibility (adjudicated), access for TK//HCG//(etc).
